#note: See @bib{RN117@814}: “The reference to mules is to the steeds that pull the sun’s chariot through the sky. They are also known from a line of an incantation in @i{Bīt rimki}: @akk{ta-(aṣ)-ṣa-an-da pa-re-ka} (var. @sux{gir₃{meš}}) @akk{ša₂ šit-mu-ru la-sa-[ma]} (var. @akk{a-la-kam}), ‘you (Šamaš) have hitched up your mules, which are ardent for running’ (cf. @bib{RN2801@57, 63}).” On the team of Šamaš’s chariot, see also @bib{RN765}. See also @bib{fromebllab0039@105}: “@i{ḫarāpu} Š means “to cause someone to be early at something”, as in the Hymn to Ninurta as Savior l. 2: @i{lā tēbâ tušaḫrap urḫa}, “Early you set on his way him who else would not rise” (@bib{RN358}; @url{/corpus/L/3/10}{eBL Corpus L III.10}). The context here suggests understanding the verb as a reference to an early sunset, rather than to dawn (cf.  @bib{RN117@460}). Alternatively, one may restore the verb as @i{erēbu} Š, “to set”, although the sign before @i{ri} is not @i{še}.”
